# Adjudication Task — Chapter 313

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃313화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|화산일학 백무성.
  6|
  7|섬서 땅에, 아니 무림에서 그 이름을 모르는 사람은 없었다.
  8|
  9|천검진인의 적전 제자이자 어린 시절부터 화산파의 미래라 불려왔던 백무성이다.
 10|
 11|귀가 밝고 말 많은 호사가(好事家)들 사이에서는 검성의 막내 제자에 관한 소문이 돌았지만, 그런 그들조차 백무성이 훗날 화산파의 장문인이 되리라는 것을 믿어 의심치 않았다.
 12|
 13|“듣자 하니 화산신룡의 무위가 이미 구파일방의 장로들을 뛰어넘었다더군. 역시 백 년에 한 번 나올까 말까 한 천재다워.”
 14|
 15|“그래도 차기 장문인은 누가 뭐라 해도 화산일학이지. 백무성은 그릇이 달라. 장문인으로서 갖춰야 할 모든 것을 타고났다고.”
 16|
 17|“그건 그렇지. 무공이 부족해, 아니면 사람이 부족해? 그가 아니라면 누가 장문인이 된단 말인가?”
 18|
 19|서안루의 일 층에서 술잔을 기울이며 대화를 나누고 있던 사람들은 알지 못했다.
 20|
 21|대화의 주인공이 자신들의 등 뒤로 지나가고 있음을.
 22|
 23|“백 대협의 위명은 익히 들었습니다. 이렇게 만나 뵙게 되어 영광입니다.”
 24|
 25|“대협이라니, 과분한 말씀 거둬 주십시오.”
 26|
 27|“아닙니다. 대협을 대협이라고 부르는 것뿐인데 무엇이 과분하다는 말씀이십니까.”
 28|
 29|호위장의 뜨거운 눈빛에 백무성은 멋쩍게 웃는 것으로 대답을 대신했다.
 30|
 31|사람들의 관심은 그에게 하루 이틀의 일이 아니다.
 32|
 33|검성 매종학의 은거 이후 주춤했던 화산파의 입지가 올라갈수록 백무성의 부담감도 더해 갔다.
 34|
 35|‘장문인이라니.’
 36|
 37|삼십 대 초반에 불과한 백무성에게는 멀고도 무거운 이름이었다.
 38|
 39|내심 고개를 내젓던 그때 호위장의 발걸음이 멈췄다.
 40|
 41|“이곳입니다.”
 42|
 43|“여기는…….”
 44|
 45|“섬서 제일이라 자부하는 저희 서안루에서도 단 한 곳밖에 없는 별채지요.”
 46|
 47|옥석(玉石)으로 장식한 정원, 온갖 고급스러운 집기로 가득 찬 내부를 둘러본 백무성이 난색을 표했다.
 48|
 49|“죄송합니다만, 별채를 이용할 만큼의 돈이 수중에 없습니다. 대신 조용한 방 하나만 내어주시겠습니까?”
 50|
 51|“하하, 역시 듣던 대로 검소하시군요.”
 52|
 53|호위장이 껄껄 웃으며 말을 이었다.
 54|
 55|“걱정하지 마십시오. 루주(樓主)께서 누누이 말씀하시길, 화산파에서 손님이 오시거든 일체의 비용도 받지 말고 극진히 모시라 하셨습니다.”
 56|
 57|“루주께서 말입니까?”
 58|
 59|“예, 작년 가을에 종남파와 모종의 문제가 있었는데, 화산파의 도움으로 잘 해결되었지요. 매화삼절(梅花三絶)의 다른 두 사제분께서 큰 활약을 해 주셨습니다.”
 60|
 61|“아, 그렇군요. 제가 폐관 수련 도중에 벌어진 일이라 잘 몰랐습니다.”
 62|
 63|“사실 저도 이야기로만 들었습니다. 근무하게 된 지 이게 겨우 달포밖에 되지 않았거든요, 하하.”
 64|
 65|백무성은 그제야 이해했다는 듯 고개를 끄덕였다.
 66|
 67|지난 일 년간 그도 놀고만 있었던 것은 아니다.
 68|
 69|천고의 기재라 할 수 있는 청풍, 그리고 진태경과의 만남은 백무성에게 있어 큰 충격인 동시에 새로운 자극이 되었다. 일 년간의 폐관 수련을 결정한 것은 그 때문이었다.
 70|
 71|‘의미 있는 시간이었지.’
 72|
 73|수련 도중 얻은 깨달음은 백무성을 전보다 더 강하고 깊이 있는 사람으로 만들어 주었다.
 74|
 75|변한 것은 그뿐만이 아니다. 화산파의 위치 또한 일 년 전에 비할 바가 아니었다.
 76|
 77|종남의 속가제자들이 대거 포진해 있는 관부조차 문제가 생기면 화산을 먼저 찾을 정도였다.
 78|
 79|‘만약 사부님께서 보낸 서신이 사실이라면 그럴 수밖에.’
 80|
 81|지금으로부터 닷새 전, 스승인 천검진인이 보낸 전서응에는 놀라운 소식이 적혀 있었다.
 82|
 83|소림에서 벌어진 혈겁, 법왕 굉도의 죽음. 그리고 수십 년만에 부활하는 신(新) 무림맹의 맹주로 검성 매종학이 물망에 오르내린다는 소식이 바로 그것이었다.
 84|
 85|“여하간 주위에서 온통 난리입니다. 제 벗들도 물어보더군요. 자식이 무공에 재능이 있는 것 같은데 화산파 속가제자로라도 들어갈 수 없겠느냐고요.”
 86|
 87|호위장의 은근한 눈빛에 담긴 뜻을 알아차린 백무성이 쓰게 웃었다.
 88|
 89|얼핏 봐도 불혹은 넘어 보이는 나이. 자식을 화산파에 입문시키고 싶은 부모의 마음은 그 또한 마찬가지이리라.
 90|
 91|하지만 백무성은 모르는 척 대답했다.
 92|
 93|“글쎄요, 인연이 닿으면 그리될 수 있겠지요. 허나 굳이 무공을 배울 필요가 있겠습니까. 그 나이에는 건강하게 자라는 것으로 족한 것을.”
 94|
 95|“……그렇습니까.”
 96|
 97|호위장의 실망한 표정에 백무성은 마음속으로 중얼거렸다.
 98|
 99|‘귀하가 곧 불어닥칠 혈풍(血風)을 알고 있다면 그런 표정은 짓지 않았을 겁니다.’
100|
101|소림의 혈겁에 관한 소문은 이미 알음알음 새어 나갔다.
102|
103|그러나 암천의 존재는 여전히 극소수만이 아는 특급 기밀. 그 몇 안 되는 이들에 속한 백무성은 직감했다.
104|
105|곧 무림에 피바람이 불어온다. 먹구름이 하늘을 가리고 수천, 수만의 병장기가 주인과 함께 땅을 뒹굴 것이다.
106|
107|부모 잃은 자식의, 자식 잃은 부모의 통곡이 사방에서 울려 퍼질 것이다.
108|
109|‘그런 일이 벌어지지 않도록 막을 겁니다. 내가, 화산이.’
110|
111|무림에 속한 모두가 백무성과 같은 마음일 터.
112|
113|갑자기 무거워진 그의 분위기에 호위장이 고개를 갸웃거리던 그때였다.
114|
115|“총관은 어디 있느냐! 총관!”
116|
117|“소협, 총관께서는 지금 잠시 자리를 비우셨습니다. 그러니 이제 고정하시고…….”
118|
119|“고정? 내가 이따위 홀대를 받았거늘, 지금 고정하게 생겼느냐!”
120|
121|“마, 말씀드렸다시피 별채는 이미 찼습니다. 특실로 안내해 드릴 테니 노여움을 가라앉히십시오.”
122|
123|“시끄럽다! 내 오늘은 반드시 별채를 써야겠으니 당장 비켜라!”
124|
125|“아이고, 소협!”
126|
127|쾅! 우지끈!
128|
129|소란스러운 소리와 함께 점점 가까워지는 고함. 호위장이 미간을 좁히며 말했다.
130|
131|“좋지 않은 모습을 보여 드려 송구스럽습니다. 제 수하들이 일을 제대로 하지 못한 모양입니다.”
132|
133|“별말씀을. 충분히 이해합니다.”
134|
135|아무리 손님을 까다롭게 가려 받더라도 서안루 또한 기루다. 꽃밭에 온갖 벌레가 끼어드는 것은 당연한 일이 아닌가.
136|
137|“그나저나 정오밖에 안 되었는데, 꽤 취한 것 같군요.”
138|
139|“종종 있는 일이지요. 어느 대갓집 자제인 것 같은데, 잘 수습해서 돌려보낼 터이니 백 대협께서는 신경 쓰지 않으셔도 됩니다.”
140|
141|백무성이 너털웃음을 지으며 고개를 저었다.
142|
143|“하하, 글쎄요. 여기 계시는 게 좋겠습니다.”
144|
145|“네?”
146|
147|“평범한 대갓집 자제는 아닌 것 같아서 말입니다.”
148|
149|“그게 무슨…….”
150|
151|의문을 표하던 호위장이 멈칫했다. 멈추지 않는 소란과 더불어 빠르게 가까워지는 인기척을 느꼈기 때문이었다.
152|
153|‘무림인!’
154|
155|점점 심상치 않게 돌아가는 상황 속, 다급한 발걸음과 함께 내원을 지키던 호위 무사들의 외침이 들렸다.
156|
157|“멈추십시오!”
158|
159|“이곳부터는 지나갈 수 없습니다!”
160|
161|서안루는 고관대작들도 드나드는 만큼 호위의 수준도 높았다. 그러나 실전 경험이 풍부한 일류 무인들인 그들조차 취객의 난동을 막기에는 역부족이었다.
162|
163|“낭인 출신 밑바닥 삼류들이 어딜 감히…….”
164|
165|“헛!”
166|
167|쉬쉭, 퍼버버벅!
168|
169|무사들의 짧은 경호성, 빠르고 강한 타격음이 울려 퍼지자 별채 밖이 삽시간에 조용해졌다.
170|
171|비틀비틀, 거친 걸음걸이가 침묵을 몰아내며 가까워지기 시작한다.
172|
173|‘저 정도로 취한 상태에서 순식간에 일류 무사 여섯을 쓰러트리다니.’
174|
175|고수, 그것도 절정 고수다.
176|
177|호위장이 굳은 얼굴로 검파에 손을 가져가려던 그때, 백무성이 작게 고개를 저어 보였다.
178|
179|“제가 나서야 할 것 같군요.”
180|
181|“백 대협, 그건…….”
182|
183|“괜찮습니다. 몇 차례 면식이 있는 사이니, 제 체면을 봐서라도 물러나 주겠지요.”
184|
185|“그 말씀은…….”
186|
187|“선대부터 내려온 인연이 있습니다. 아, 물론…….”
188|
189|백무성이 볼을 긁적이며 한마디를 덧붙였다.
190|
191|“그리 썩, 화목한 인연은 아니지만 말입니다.”
192|
193|“……!”
194|
195|그때 호위장의 뇌리에 번개처럼 스치는 생각이 있었다.
196|
197|하나는 종남파라는 세 글자. 그리고 그 뒤를 이어 떠오른 것은 한 사람의 이름이었다.
198|
199|“호, 혹시?”
200|
201|서안루의 호위장이 된 지 이제 겨우 보름 남짓. 하지만 그 사람에 관한 소문은 귀에 못이 박히도록 들었다.
202|
203|종남파라는 출신만큼이나 대단한 성미의 소유자.
204|
205|표정을 일그러트린 호위장이 한 사람의 이름을 말하려던 순간이었다.
206|
207|꽈앙!
208|
209|단단한 흑목(黑木)으로 만들어진 별채의 문이 박살 나며 나뭇조각이 사방으로 튀었다.
210|
211|비틀거리는 걸음걸이, 불콰하게 달아오른 얼굴의 청년을 향해 백무성이 싱긋 웃어 보였다.
212|
213|“오랜만이군. 잘 지냈나?”
214|
215|그와 동시에.
216|
217|“당신이 왜 여기 있지?”
218|
219|종남일룡(綜南一龍) 혁소평의 얼굴이 악귀처럼 일그러졌다.
220|
221|
222|
223|* * *
224|
225|
226|
227|“와아! 와아아!”
228|
229|“제발 소리 지르지 마. 사람들이 다 쳐다보잖아.”
230|
231|“은인! 저기 당과!”
232|
233|“그놈의 당과는 시부럴 거. 당과 안 질려?”
234|
235|“네!”
236|
237|“그럼 그냥 아예 가게를 차려!”
238|
239|“그럼 당과 장수 아저씨랑 사천까지 같이 가도 돼요?”
240|
241|“아니, 미친…….”
242|
243|“저기 소면 팔아요! 소고기로 육수를 냈대요!”
244|
245|청풍 너란 새끼. 어디로 튈지 모르는 탱탱볼 같은 새끼…….
246|
247|나는 길거리 좌판을 향해 쪼르르 달려가던 청풍의 뒷덜미를 재빨리 낚아챘다.
248|
249|“제발 더도 말고 덜도 말고 사람답게만 살자. 사람답게!”
250|
251|“당과, 소면…….”
252|
253|“아, 조금만 참으면 배 터지게 먹여 준다고!”
254|
255|“정말요?”
256|
257|“몇 번을 말했잖아. 그러니까 제발 입 다물고, 조용히 따라와라. 응?”
258|
259|물론 내 돈으로 먹이는 게 아니라 화산파 돈이지만, 엎어치나 메치나 거기서 거기지 뭐.
260|
261|‘원래는 여기도 그냥 지나갔어야 했는데.’
262|
263|본래 일정대로라면 서안에 들를 필요조차 없었다.
264|
265|하지만 떠나기 전 화산파 장문인인 천검진인으로부터 서안에 들러 달라는 부탁도 받았고, 청풍의 고향이니 겸사겸사 지나가게 되었을 뿐이다.
266|
267|칠주야 가까이 제대로 먹지도, 씻지도 않은 채 강행군을 했으니 하루만이라도 대접받으며 푹 쉬고 싶기도 했다.
268|
269|‘화산일학 백무성이 기다리고 있다고 했었는데.’
270|
271|그를 마지막으로 본 것이 벌써 일 년도 넘었다.
272|
273|적천강을 따라 안휘로 떠나기 전, 백무성이 내게 그런 말을 했었다.
274|
275|
276|
277|‘언제든지 섬서에 오면 연락 주십시오. 제가 제대로 대접하지요. 하하.’

“Gah!”

“I think I should handle this.”

“Great Hero Baek, that’s—”

“……!”

*This kind of shit makes me sick of being a martial artist.*

But the existence of Dark Heaven remained a top-secret known only to a handful of people. As one of those few, Baek Museong could sense what was coming.

[P51]
A bloody wind would soon sweep through the Murim. Dark clouds would cover the sky, and thousands—tens of thousands—of weapons would lie scattered across the ground beside their owners.

[P52]
The wails of children who had lost their parents and parents who had lost their children would echo from every direction.

[P53]
*I’ll stop that from happening. I will—and Huashan will.*

[P54]
Surely everyone in the Murim felt the same.

[P55]
The Captain of the Guards was tilting his head at the sudden heaviness in Baek Museong’s expression when—

[P56]
“Where is the chief manager? Chief Manager!”

[P57]
“Young Hero, the chief manager has stepped away for a moment. So please, calm yourself—”

[P58]
“Calm myself? After being treated with such disrespect, do I look like I’m in any state to calm down?”

[P59]
“A-as I explained, the private annex is already occupied. We’ll show you to a special room, so please calm down.”

[P60]
“Shut up! I must have the private annex today, so get out of my way!”

[P61]
“Oh, Young Hero!”

[P62]
*Bang! Crack!*

[P63]
The shouting drew closer amid the clamor. The Captain of the Guards knitted his brows.

[P64]
“I apologize for showing you such an unpleasant scene. It seems my subordinates have failed to handle the matter properly.”

[P65]
“Please, think nothing of it. I understand completely.”

[P66]
No matter how carefully Xi’an Tower selected its guests, it was still a pleasure house. All sorts of insects were bound to swarm a flower garden.

[P67]
“Still, it’s barely noon, and he already sounds quite drunk.”

[P68]
“It happens from time to time. He appears to be the son of some powerful family, but we’ll settle the matter and send him home. Great Hero Baek, you needn’t concern yourself.”

[P69]
Baek Museong laughed and shook his head.

[P70]
“Haha, I’m not so sure. You’d better remain here.”

[P71]
“Pardon?”

[P72]
“He doesn’t seem to be an ordinary scion of a powerful family.”

[P73]
“What do you mean…?”

[P74]
The Captain of the Guards faltered. Amid the continuing uproar, he had sensed someone approaching rapidly.

[P75]
*A martial artist!*

[P76]
As the situation took a more serious turn, hurried footsteps sounded, followed by shouts from the guards protecting the inner courtyard.

[P77]
“Stop!”

[P78]
“You cannot pass beyond this point!”

[P79]
Xi’an Tower was frequented by high officials and powerful nobles, so the quality of its guards was correspondingly high. Yet even those battle-tested First Rate martial artists were no match for the drunken man’s rampage.

[P80]
“You lowly Third Rate trash from wandering martial artist backgrounds dare…”

[P81]
“Hah!”

[P82]
*Whoosh! Thud-thud-thud!*

[P83]
The guards’ short cries of exertion and the quick, powerful sounds of impacts rang out. In an instant, the area outside the private annex fell silent.

[P84]
Then rough, unsteady footsteps approached, driving away the silence.

[P85]
*He took down six First Rate martial artists in an instant while that drunk?*

[P86]
*A master—and not just any master. A Peak master.*

[P87]
Just as the Captain of the Guards’ face hardened and his hand moved toward his sword hilt, Baek Museong gave a small shake of his head.

[P88]
“I think I should handle this.”

[P89]
“Great Hero Baek, that’s…”

[P90]
“It’s all right. We’ve met several times before. He’ll back down for my sake, if nothing else.”

[P91]
“You mean…?”

[P92]
“Our connection goes back several generations. Ah, of course…”

[P93]
Baek Museong scratched his cheek and added,

[P94]
“It isn’t exactly a harmonious connection.”

[P95]
“……!”

[P96]
At that moment, a thought flashed through the Captain of the Guards’ mind like lightning.

[P97]
First came the words *Zhongnan Sect*. Then the name of a man.

[P98]
“C-could it be?”

[P99]
He had only been the Captain of the Guards at Xi’an Tower for a little over two weeks, but he had already heard so many rumors about that man that his ears ached.

[P100]
A man whose temperament was every bit as formidable as his pedigree.

[P101]
The Captain of the Guards grimaced and was about to speak the man’s name when—

[P102]
*Boom!*

[P103]
The door of the private annex, made from sturdy blackwood, exploded. Splinters flew in every direction.

[P104]
Baek Museong smiled at the young man who staggered inside, his face flushed red with drink.

[P105]
“It’s been a long time. Have you been well?”

[P106]
At the same moment, the young man snarled.

[P107]
“Why are you here?”

[P108]
The face of Hyuk Sopyung, the Zhongnan One Dragon,[^1] twisted like that of a fiend.

[P109]
* * *

[P110]
“Wow! Wowww!”

[P111]
“Please stop shouting. Everyone’s staring.”

[P112]
“Benefactor! Candied fruit over there!”

[P113]
“That damn candied fruit. Aren’t you sick of it yet?”

[P114]
“No!”

[P115]
“Then just open your own shop!”

[P116]
“Can the candied-fruit vendor come with us all the way to Sichuan?”

[P117]
“No, you lunatic…”

[P118]
“They sell noodles over there! They say the broth is made with beef!”

[P119]
Cheongpung, you little bastard. You’re like a rubber ball that could bounce off in any direction without warning…

[P120]
I quickly grabbed Cheongpung by the back of his neck as he scampered toward a roadside food stall.

[P121]
“Please, let’s just act like human beings. That’s all I’m asking. Like human beings!”

[P122]
“Candied fruit… noodles…”

[P123]
“Just wait a little longer, and I’ll feed you until your belly bursts!”

[P124]
“Really?”

[P125]
“How many times do I have to say it? So please shut your mouth and follow me quietly, okay?”

[P126]
Of course, I wouldn’t be feeding him with my money. It would be Huashan’s money, but that was all the same in the end.

[P127]
*We were supposed to pass straight through here, too.*

[P128]
According to our original schedule, there hadn’t been any need to stop in Xi’an at all.

[P129]
But before we left, Heavenly Sword True Person, the Sect Leader of Huashan, had asked us to stop by Xi’an. Since it was Cheongpung’s hometown, we had decided to pass through while we were at it.

[P130]
We had been pushing ourselves for nearly seven days and nights without eating or washing properly. I also wanted to enjoy some hospitality and get at least one full day of rest.

[P131]
*I was told Huashan’s Lone Crane, Baek Museong, would be waiting for us.*

[P132]
It had already been more than a year since I’d last seen him.

[P133]
Before I left for Anhui with Jeok Cheongang, Baek Museong had said this to me.

[P134]
*“Contact me whenever you come to Shaanxi. I’ll give you the full-course treatment. Haha.”*

[P135]
When he promised me the full course, I’d wondered if the guy was from Busan, but apparently it hadn’t been empty talk.

[P136]
Not if we were meeting like this today.

[P137]
“By the way, where’s Xi’an Tower?”

[P138]
A passerby I’d stopped had told me we only needed to follow the main road straight ahead. But why was the street so crowded? I couldn’t see the end of it.

[P139]
As I looked around, a finger caked in black grime pointed toward a building in the distance.

[P140]
“That is Xi’an Tower.”

[P141]
“Where? Oh, you’re right. How did you know?”

[P142]
Gung Gibang, the future boss of all beggars, answered proudly.

[P143]
“It is the finest place to beg. Even the food they leave behind and throw away is fit for a sumptuous feast, and because people of high status come and go, they give plenty of alms. Every beggar knows this place.”

[P144]
“……”

[P145]
So it was a Beggars’ Sect hotspot.

[P146]
I shook my head and headed toward Xi’an Tower.

[P147]
When we reached its enormous main entrance, wide enough for ten people to pass through side by side, a guard who appeared to belong to Xi’an Tower bowed his head.

[P148]
“I’m sorry, but we’re closed today.”

[P149]
“……What? Is it a day off?”

[P150]
“Not exactly. A slight problem arose during business hours.”

[P151]
“Oh.”

[P152]
I hadn’t expected that.

[P153]
I glanced to the side and saw Cheongpung looking as though he was about to burst into tears.

[P154]
Scratching my head, I spoke to the guard.

[P155]
“Isn’t there any way around it? We had an appointment today. The man’s name is Baek Museong. He said you’d know if we gave you his name.”

[P156]
“Again, I’m sorry, but at the moment— Excuse me? Did you say Great Hero Baek Museong?”

[P157]
“Yes. Baek Museong, Huashan’s Lone Crane.”

[P158]
Cheongpung called out desperately.

[P159]
“Martial Nephew Baek! Where are you, Martial Nephew Baek? Can you hear my stomach growling?”

[P160]
The guard looked back and forth between us, then flung open the tightly closed main gate.

[P161]
“I’ll escort you to the private annex immediately!”

[P162]
*What the hell?*

[P163]
*Why the sudden change in attitude?*

[P164]
*Did Baek Museong stand us up?*

[P165]
My guess was wrong.

[P166]
We followed the guard as he raced ahead almost fast enough to fly and arrived at a nearly devastated private annex.

[P167]
Baek Museong was waiting for us there, sword drawn.

[P168]
*Wow. This really is the full course.*

[P169]
*This kind of shit makes me sick of being a martial artist.*

[P170]
[^1]: A sobriquet for a leading young martial artist of the Zhongnan Sect.
```

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

“Hah!”

[P88]

[P90]

[P94]

[P95]

[P98]
“C-could it be?”

[P100]

[P105]

[P107]

[P109]

[P110]
“Wow! Wowww!”

[P111]
“Please stop shouting. Everyone’s staring.”

[P113]

[P114]
“No!”

“Just wait a little longer, and I’ll feed you until your belly bursts!”

“Really?”

[P128]

[P129]

[P130]

[P131]
*I was told Huashan’s Lone Crane, Baek Museong, would be waiting for us.*

[P132]
It had already been more than a year since I’d last seen him.

[P133]

[P134]
*“Contact me whenever you come to Shaanxi. I’ll give you the full-course treatment. Haha.”*

[P135]

[P136]
Not if we were meeting like this today.

[P137]
“By the way, where’s Xi’an Tower?”

[P138]
A passerby I’d stopped had told me we only needed to follow the main road straight ahead. But why was the street so crowded? I couldn’t see the end of it.

[P139]
As I looked around, a finger caked in black grime pointed toward a building in the distance.

[P140]
“That is Xi’an Tower.”

[P141]
“Where? Oh, you’re right. How did you know?”

[P142]
Gung Gibang, the future boss of all beggars, answered proudly.

[P143]
“It is the finest place to beg. Even the food they leave behind and throw away is fit for a sumptuous feast, and because people of high status come and go, they give plenty of alms. Every beggar knows this place.”

[P144]
“……”

[P145]
So it was a Beggars’ Sect hotspot.

[P146]
I shook my head and headed toward Xi’an Tower.

[P147]
When we reached its enormous main entrance, wide enough for ten people to pass through side by side, a guard who appeared to belong to Xi’an Tower bowed his head.

[P148]
“I’m sorry, but we’re closed today.”

[P149]
“……What? Is it a day off?”

[P150]
“Not exactly. A slight problem arose during business hours.”

[P151]
“Oh.”

[P152]
I hadn’t expected that.

[P153]
I glanced to the side and saw Cheongpung looking as though he was about to burst into tears.

[P154]
Scratching my head, I spoke to the guard.

[P155]
“Isn’t there any way around it? We had an appointment today. The man’s name is Baek Museong. He said you’d know if we gave you his name.”

[P156]
“Again, I’m sorry, but at the moment— Excuse me? Did you say Great Hero Baek Museong?”

[P157]
“Yes. Baek Museong, Huashan’s Lone Crane.”

[P158]
Cheongpung called out desperately.

[P159]
“Martial Nephew Baek! Where are you, Martial Nephew Baek? Can you hear my stomach growling?”

[P160]
The guard looked back and forth between us, then flung open the tightly closed main gate.

[P161]
“I’ll escort you to the private annex immediately!”

[P162]
*What the hell?*

[P163]
*Why the sudden change in attitude?*

[P164]
*Did Baek Museong stand us up?*

[P165]
My guess was wrong.

[P166]
We followed the guard as he raced ahead almost fast enough to fly and arrived at a nearly devastated private annex.

[P167]
Baek Museong was waiting for us there, sword drawn.

[P168]
*Wow. This really is the full course.*

[P169]
*This kind of shit makes me sick of being a martial artist.*

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.

Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 313

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃313화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|화산일학 백무성.
  6|
  7|섬서 땅에, 아니 무림에서 그 이름을 모르는 사람은 없었다.
  8|
  9|천검진인의 적전 제자이자 어린 시절부터 화산파의 미래라 불려왔던 백무성이다.
 10|
 11|귀가 밝고 말 많은 호사가(好事家)들 사이에서는 검성의 막내 제자에 관한 소문이 돌았지만, 그런 그들조차 백무성이 훗날 화산파의 장문인이 되리라는 것을 믿어 의심치 않았다.
 12|
 13|“듣자 하니 화산신룡의 무위가 이미 구파일방의 장로들을 뛰어넘었다더군. 역시 백 년에 한 번 나올까 말까 한 천재다워.”
 14|
 15|“그래도 차기 장문인은 누가 뭐라 해도 화산일학이지. 백무성은 그릇이 달라. 장문인으로서 갖춰야 할 모든 것을 타고났다고.”
 16|
 17|“그건 그렇지. 무공이 부족해, 아니면 사람이 부족해? 그가 아니라면 누가 장문인이 된단 말인가?”
 18|
 19|서안루의 일 층에서 술잔을 기울이며 대화를 나누고 있던 사람들은 알지 못했다.
 20|
 21|대화의 주인공이 자신들의 등 뒤로 지나가고 있음을.
 22|
 23|“백 대협의 위명은 익히 들었습니다. 이렇게 만나 뵙게 되어 영광입니다.”
 24|
 25|“대협이라니, 과분한 말씀 거둬 주십시오.”
 26|
 27|“아닙니다. 대협을 대협이라고 부르는 것뿐인데 무엇이 과분하다는 말씀이십니까.”
 28|
 29|호위장의 뜨거운 눈빛에 백무성은 멋쩍게 웃는 것으로 대답을 대신했다.
 30|
 31|사람들의 관심은 그에게 하루 이틀의 일이 아니다.
 32|
 33|검성 매종학의 은거 이후 주춤했던 화산파의 입지가 올라갈수록 백무성의 부담감도 더해 갔다.
 34|
 35|‘장문인이라니.’
 36|
 37|삼십 대 초반에 불과한 백무성에게는 멀고도 무거운 이름이었다.
 38|
 39|내심 고개를 내젓던 그때 호위장의 발걸음이 멈췄다.
 40|
 41|“이곳입니다.”
 42|
 43|“여기는…….”
 44|
 45|“섬서 제일이라 자부하는 저희 서안루에서도 단 한 곳밖에 없는 별채지요.”
 46|
 47|옥석(玉石)으로 장식한 정원, 온갖 고급스러운 집기로 가득 찬 내부를 둘러본 백무성이 난색을 표했다.
 48|
 49|“죄송합니다만, 별채를 이용할 만큼의 돈이 수중에 없습니다. 대신 조용한 방 하나만 내어주시겠습니까?”
 50|
 51|“하하, 역시 듣던 대로 검소하시군요.”
 52|
 53|호위장이 껄껄 웃으며 말을 이었다.
 54|
 55|“걱정하지 마십시오. 루주(樓主)께서 누누이 말씀하시길, 화산파에서 손님이 오시거든 일체의 비용도 받지 말고 극진히 모시라 하셨습니다.”
 56|
 57|“루주께서 말입니까?”
 58|
 59|“예, 작년 가을에 종남파와 모종의 문제가 있었는데, 화산파의 도움으로 잘 해결되었지요. 매화삼절(梅花三絶)의 다른 두 사제분께서 큰 활약을 해 주셨습니다.”
 60|
 61|“아, 그렇군요. 제가 폐관 수련 도중에 벌어진 일이라 잘 몰랐습니다.”
 62|
 63|“사실 저도 이야기로만 들었습니다. 근무하게 된 지 이게 겨우 달포밖에 되지 않았거든요, 하하.”
 64|
 65|백무성은 그제야 이해했다는 듯 고개를 끄덕였다.
 66|
 67|지난 일 년간 그도 놀고만 있었던 것은 아니다.
 68|
 69|천고의 기재라 할 수 있는 청풍, 그리고 진태경과의 만남은 백무성에게 있어 큰 충격인 동시에 새로운 자극이 되었다. 일 년간의 폐관 수련을 결정한 것은 그 때문이었다.
 70|
 71|‘의미 있는 시간이었지.’
 72|
 73|수련 도중 얻은 깨달음은 백무성을 전보다 더 강하고 깊이 있는 사람으로 만들어 주었다.
 74|
 75|변한 것은 그뿐만이 아니다. 화산파의 위치 또한 일 년 전에 비할 바가 아니었다.
 76|
 77|종남의 속가제자들이 대거 포진해 있는 관부조차 문제가 생기면 화산을 먼저 찾을 정도였다.
 78|
 79|‘만약 사부님께서 보낸 서신이 사실이라면 그럴 수밖에.’
 80|
 81|지금으로부터 닷새 전, 스승인 천검진인이 보낸 전서응에는 놀라운 소식이 적혀 있었다.
 82|
 83|소림에서 벌어진 혈겁, 법왕 굉도의 죽음. 그리고 수십 년만에 부활하는 신(新) 무림맹의 맹주로 검성 매종학이 물망에 오르내린다는 소식이 바로 그것이었다.
 84|
 85|“여하간 주위에서 온통 난리입니다. 제 벗들도 물어보더군요. 자식이 무공에 재능이 있는 것 같은데 화산파 속가제자로라도 들어갈 수 없겠느냐고요.”
 86|
 87|호위장의 은근한 눈빛에 담긴 뜻을 알아차린 백무성이 쓰게 웃었다.
 88|
 89|얼핏 봐도 불혹은 넘어 보이는 나이. 자식을 화산파에 입문시키고 싶은 부모의 마음은 그 또한 마찬가지이리라.
 90|
 91|하지만 백무성은 모르는 척 대답했다.
 92|
 93|“글쎄요, 인연이 닿으면 그리될 수 있겠지요. 허나 굳이 무공을 배울 필요가 있겠습니까. 그 나이에는 건강하게 자라는 것으로 족한 것을.”
 94|
 95|“……그렇습니까.”
 96|
 97|호위장의 실망한 표정에 백무성은 마음속으로 중얼거렸다.
 98|
 99|‘귀하가 곧 불어닥칠 혈풍(血風)을 알고 있다면 그런 표정은 짓지 않았을 겁니다.’
100|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

{

"decisions": [

"hunk_id": "H001",

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
